fields.hero_description: Create a silent auction form that gives every item its own bid page and QR code, then names the winners at close.
fields.features_heading: What Paper Bid Sheets Leave to Volunteers
fields.features_subheading: A clipboard collects names and amounts. These six pieces handle what volunteers would otherwise check by hand.
fields.feature_1:
Bids checked against the high bid

Set an opening bid and a minimum increment for each item. Any bid under the current high plus that increment goes back to the guest with the lowest amount that would count.
fields.feature_2:
A QR code on every bid card

Print a QR code for each item on its table card. Guests scan it with a phone and type a bidder number and an amount. The bid lands in the one table that every item shares.
fields.feature_3:
Item intake with photos and value

Collect donated items through a form that asks for a photo, the fair market value, and any expiry date. Each submission becomes a numbered catalog entry the committee can sort.
fields.feature_4:
Outbid emails during online auctions

Email a bidder the moment someone tops their bid, with the new high and a button to bid again. A week-long auction keeps people returning with no volunteer chasing them.
fields.feature_5:
Winner emails that state item value

Put the winning bid for each item beside the value listed in its catalog entry. Every winner gets one email that shows both numbers for each item they won, for their records.
fields.feature_6:
Your code on GitHub when you want it

Export the full codebase to your own GitHub repository on paid plans once the auction grows into a year-round donor portal. The code is yours to change from then on.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Groups That Take Bids Online
fields.tab_content_1:
A $340 bid bounces when $350 is the floor

The Hollis Park Elementary spring gala puts 60 items on its tables, each with a QR code on its bid card. The Pine Lake cabin weekend sits at $325 with a $25 increment. A parent who enters $340 is asked to bid at least $350, and the bids table only ever holds valid bids.
fields.tab_content_2:
The donor's own value sets each opening bid

Donors fill in the value themselves when they give an item to the Cedar Hills Hospital Foundation gala, and each one uploads a photo. No opening bid is more than 40% of the stated value. A spa day valued at $500 opens at $200.
fields.tab_content_3:
Someone tops your bid and the email names the new high

Willow Creek Animal Rescue keeps its online auction open for 7 days. Tessa Okafor had $165 on a handmade quilt until another bidder went to $180. Tessa got an email with the new high bid and a link to the quilt, where $190 retakes the lead.
fields.tab_content_4:
Bidding stops and each winner gets a pickup list

The Oak Valley Church fall festival closes its silent auction at 9:00 pm. The top bid on each of its 42 items becomes the winning bid. Every winner gets one email listing their items and the pickup table. Maria Ortiz won 3 items for $410 and collects them at table 4.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Silent Auction Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to set up a silent auction form and test every bid rule before guests arrive.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose paper, a form or both
fields.howto_step_1_des: Paper bid sheets suit a room of 40 guests and a dozen items. Once the item count climbs, or bidding runs online for days, a form does the tallying for you. Keep a few printed sheets on hand as a backup.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each donated item a number, a short description, a photo, and the donor's name. Record the fair market value the donor states, plus any expiry date or restriction, such as dinner reservations valid on weeknights only.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide how opening bids and increments are set before the catalog goes out. Open each item at no more than half of its fair market value. Round increments to a clean $10 or $25 so guests can do the math standing up.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the item list and your bidding rules into one prompt. Emergent builds a bid page for every item and the bids table behind them, plus a view for the committee. Ask for a new increment or a later close and the form changes.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Print one QR code per item
fields.howto_step_5_des: Print each item's QR code on its table card, with the item number large enough to read from a step away. Online auctions skip the cards and send one catalog link by email and on your social pages instead.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set the close and the winner email
fields.howto_step_6_des: Set the closing time to the minute and write the email winners receive. Name the pickup table and the hours volunteers staff it. Show each item's stated value next to the winning bid for the winner's records.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run a test auction from two phones
fields.howto_step_7_des: Bid on one test item from two phones a day before the event. Try an amount under the increment, then let one phone top the other and check that the outbid email arrives. Close the test item and read the winner email.

faq_plan.q: What are some items to avoid at silent auctions?
faq_plan.ref: What are some items to avoid at silent auctions?

prov.original: What are some items to avoid at silent auctions?

faq_plan.a: Start with clothing, highly personal artwork, vintage or antique pieces, and vouchers for everyday services such as accounting or haircuts: one auction platform's guide names each as a likely flop. Clothing has to fit the winner, and the guide suggests a gift voucher to a clothing store instead. It also warns that bidders are less likely to want items with a lot of strings attached.

faq_plan.q: How to create a silent auction sheet?
faq_plan.ref: How to create a silent auction sheet?

prov.original: How to create a silent auction sheet?

faq_plan.a: Put the item number and name at the top, then a short description, the item's value, the starting bid, and the minimum increment. Add numbered lines below for bidder numbers and amounts, with the closing time at the foot. To skip paper, describe your items to Emergent's AI form builder, and it builds a bid page for each item plus one table of every bid.

faq_plan.q: What should silent auction forms ask bidders when they register?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a name and a phone number or email, then assign a bidder number at check-in. Guests write or type that number on each bid, which keeps bids short and names off the public sheet. Take that contact detail at check-in, since outbid notices and the winner email go there.

faq_plan.q: Can I put a silent auction form template online?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Each column on a silent auction form template becomes a field online, and the blank bidder lines become one bid box. The online version can also check the amount against the increment before it counts. Keep gifts with no item attached, such as pledges during a paddle raise, on a separate donation form apart from the winning bids.

faq_plan.q: Can two bids tie on a silent auction bid form?
faq_plan.a: Not on a digital form that enforces the increment. A bid equal to the current high falls below the high plus the increment, and the form returns it to the guest. On paper, two guests can write the same amount on consecutive lines. Settle that before the event by printing a rule on each sheet, such as the first line with that amount wins.

faq_plan.q: What bid increment should a silent auction item have?
faq_plan.a: Scale it with the item's value. One auction platform's guide suggests $5-10 for items under $100, $10-25 for items valued $100-500, and $25-50 or more for items over $500. Emergent changes the increment on any item when you ask for it in a prompt, even after the catalog is live.

faq_plan.q: How do I sell event T-shirts at a silent auction without bidding?
faq_plan.a: Sell them at a fixed price through a separate order form, not the auction form guests bid on. A shirt has to fit the buyer, and a uniform order form asks each person for a size and a quantity before anything is printed. Separate tables also keep shirt sales out of the winner totals.

faq_plan.q: How do I show a silent auction item's high bid without naming the bidder?
faq_plan.a: Show the amount and the bid count, and leave the bidder off the public page. The app Emergent builds can list each item's current high bid and number of bids, while bidder numbers stay in the committee view. Guests see what they have to beat, and only volunteers see who holds the lead.

faq_plan.q: What should the opening bid be on a donated silent auction item?
faq_plan.a: Roughly a third to a half of its value. One fundraising platform's guide sets starting bids between about a third and a half of retail value. Another suggests about a third of fair market value, closer to half for unique or high-demand items. Record each item's value at intake, and every opening bid can be worked out from it.

faq_plan.q: What value should a donated service get on a silent auction form?
faq_plan.a: Use the price the business would charge a paying customer for the same work. Ask for that figure when the service is donated, and list it as the item's value. For a service such as catering, a short quote form gets the scope and the price in writing before the catalog goes out. That figure then sets the item's opening bid.
